headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors from shared file-based workflows; Aider’s git-write defaults can also conflict with next-ai-draw-io’s MCP/API-driven document processing.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Aider reads and writes repo files and shared git history, while next-ai-draw-io ingests PDFs, text, images, and diagrams via natural-language commands and MCP. That creates a plausible file-based instruction bridge even without a documented direct channel. The interaction is inferred from both profiles, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or exported files, content from one can be parsed as instructions by the other.
IF next-ai-draw-io ingests Aider-authored text or diagrams without provenance checks, prompt injection becomes feasible.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and repos for the two agents.
Disable automatic ingestion of untrusted text/diagram files.
Add a manual review step before either agent consumes the other's output.
Use provenance labels on generated files and prompts.
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and trust-boundary checks in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Aider touches source code and git history and can egress broadly to configured model providers; next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, images, and diagrams and also has broad network egress. If they share a workspace or API credentials, sensitive file contents can flow into external inference services. The profiles support the pathway, but not a direct leak proof, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents access the same repository or document folder, sensitive source files can be exposed to both.
IF either agent sends file contents to configured model providers, those contents may leave the local environment.
mitigations: Keep code and document corpora in separate directories.
Use separate API keys and principals for each agent.
Restrict outbound network access to approved endpoints only.
Redact secrets before either agent processes shared files.
requires-engineering: add DLP or egress allowlisting at the orchestrator boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Aider can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and broad network egress. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, they can race on files, commits, or externally triggered actions. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit in A and B has write-adjacent MCP/API behavior, the default-risk ceiling is high.
conditions: IF both agents are attached to the same git repo or shared document set, concurrent edits can overwrite each other.
IF next-ai-draw-io uses MCP tools against mutable resources while Aider is committing changes, state divergence can occur.
mitigations: Run the agents on separate branches or separate repos.
Serialize access with a lock or queue.
Require manual merge review before commits land.
Disable MCP actions that mutate shared resources during Aider sessions.
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks and conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Aider produces code and git commits that next-ai-draw-io could ingest as authoritative text or diagrams, while next-ai-draw-io can transform inputs through natural-language visualization and MCP. That creates a plausible chain where one agent’s output becomes the other’s input without verification. The blast radius is multiple work products, but not clearly irreversible, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes Aider-generated files as source-of-truth, downstream diagrams or summaries can inherit errors.
IF Aider commits unverified content that next-ai-draw-io later republishes, mistakes cascade across artifacts.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Mark one agent’s outputs as draft-only until reviewed.
Compare generated artifacts against source files before publishing.
Limit next-ai-draw-io to read-only rendering for Aider outputs.
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware validation between generation and publication.

E_compliance.rationale: Aider explicitly handles model-provider API keys and source code/git history; next-ai-draw-io handles API keys and document/image content. The profiles do not show a residency or certification mismatch, so only a modest compliance gap is evidenced. Because the pairwise compliance pathway is not documented, this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into either agent without a matching policy, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or logging settings differ between the two configured model providers, records-handling mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows.
Review provider retention settings for both agents.
Use separate accounts with documented data-processing terms.
Minimize logging of prompts and file contents.
requires-engineering: formalize residency and retention controls per data class.
